title: Potential DOM XSS via unsanitized error message in innerHTML
claim: The catch block inserts error details into the DOM using innerHTML without sanitization. If an attacker can trigger an error where the error message or stack contains user-controlled content, this could lead to DOM-based cross-site scripting.
evidence:
The code uses: container.innerHTML = `
Error: ${e}
Stack: ${e.stack}
`; Both e and e.stack are interpolated directly into HTML.
trigger: An attacker supplies input that causes a runtime error whose message contains malicious HTML/script (e.g., through a JSON parse error that includes raw input, or a failed fetch that echoes a URL). When the catch executes, the malicious content is rendered as HTML.
impact: Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the application, potentially leading to session hijacking, data theft, or account takeover.
test_implication: Add a test that simulates an error with a message containing '' and verifies that no alert is triggered and the text is displayed as plain text.
suggested_verification: Manually cause an error with a malicious message (e.g., by manipulating input that appears in error output) and observe whether it is rendered as HTML or text.

title: Exposing internal game objects globally for debugging
claim: The entry point attaches model, controller, and view instances to the global window object for debugging purposes. This exposes internal state and methods to any script running on the page, increasing the attack surface in a production environment.
evidence: The code sets: window.gameModel = model; window.gameController = controller; window.gameView = view; with the comment 'Expose for debugging (optional)'.
trigger: If the application is deployed with debugging exposed, an attacker who can inject or execute any script (e.g., via a separate XSS) can directly manipulate game state or invoke controller methods, potentially bypassing intended logic.
impact: Loss of integrity of game state and potentially enabling cheats or disruptions, as well as facilitating further exploitation if combined with other vulnerabilities.
test_implication: Ensure that in production builds or when a debug flag is not set, these globals are not defined. Test that the globals are absent or inaccessible.
suggested_verification: Check if the code includes a mechanism to conditionally expose these globals only in development (e.g., based on environment variable or build flag). If not, consider removing or guarding them.
suggested_fix: Remove the exposure in production or guard it with a condition: if (DEBUG) { window.gameModel = model; ... } or use a more controlled debugging mechanism that does not expose full object references.

title: Scripts executed before footer element is parsed may cause DOM access errors
claim: The footer element (#app-footer) appears after the script tags; scripts execute immediately when encountered, so any attempt to access the footer will fail.
evidence: Lines 32-35 load gameModel.js, gameController.js, gameView.js, main.js. Line 36 begins <footer id="app-footer">. Without defer or async, scripts execute synchronously before parsing continues, leaving the footer undefined.
trigger: Any code in the loaded scripts that references document.getElementById('app-footer') or otherwise tries to manipulate the footer.
impact: Potential JavaScript runtime error, preventing game initialization or footer functionality.
test_implication: Verify whether scripts depend on footer; test page load in browser and monitor console for errors.
suggested_verification: Search script files for references to 'app-footer' or footer element; run application and check if footer-related features work.
suggested_fix: Move script tags after the footer element (just before closing body) or add defer attribute and handle DOMContentLoaded in scripts.
